raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Large k-pool prefills repeat indexer logits and top-k on every attention TP rank.

## Modifications

`SGLANG_OPT_USE_DSA_KPOOL_PREFILL_TP=1`, off by default, splits query rows across those ranks and gathers the indices. Existing configs do not change. The gate needs at least 4096 rows, and rows times pooled keys of at least 100 million. Context parallelism, scattered inputs, and graph capture stay replicated.

## Accuracy Tests

A registered test runs the real plan method on NCCL ranks at TP4 with synthetic inputs and compares sharded with replicated rows. It fails on a wrong offset or size, a lost row, a closed gate, a missing scattered check, or a rank over its share.

Validation on `70af701411`: this test on 4 B200s, one manual TP2 run, flag-off k-pool tests, and a RAGGED and PAGED probe at TP2 and TP4.

GSM8K and server numbers come from `f9b571c3b8`, with the same query rows and gather. GSM8K prompts do not open the gate. Long prompts do, and their greedy answers matched across instances.

```bash
# GLM-5.3-Flash FP8, 4 B200s, two instances per arm, with and without SGLANG_OPT_USE_DSA_KPOOL_PREFILL_TP=1
# test_glm53_flash_b200 low-latency recipe
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 weights> --tp-size 4 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend trtllm --dsa-decode-backend trtllm --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm --reasoning-parser auto --tool-call-parser auto \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6
sgl-eval run gsm8k --num-examples 200 --num-threads 64 --max-tokens 32768 \
  --temperature 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --thinking
```

Not verified on this head: full-model serving, DP2 x TP2, symmetric memory. Never verified: TP8, MSCCL++, full-model TP2, ROCm (gate opens there), other GPUs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Server ranges overlap at each size. In plan rows, flag on is faster only at 16384 x 16384. On `70af701411`, a fresh process's first flag-on gather took 1.1 to 1.8 s at TP4 and 0.45 to 0.82 s at TP2, or under 6 ms after one earlier `all_gather` on the same group.

| Case (rows x pooled keys), flag on/off | TP4 | TP2 | Gate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| sgl-eval 0.1.3 gsm8k | 97.0%, 98.5% / 98.5%, 98.5% | not run | closed |
| Server, 35,844 tokens (s), one value per instance, each the median of 5 flushed-cache requests with 1 output token | 0.80, 0.95 (mean 0.875) / 0.81, 0.81 (mean 0.81), about 8% higher | not run | open |
| Server, 74,314 tokens (s) | 1.65, 1.71 (mean 1.68) / 1.93, 1.66 (mean 1.795), about 6% lower | not run | open |
| Server, 141,994 tokens (s) | 3.06, 3.21 (mean 3.135) / 3.33, 3.15 (mean 3.24), about 3% lower | not run | open |
| Plan method on `70af701411`, scratch harness, synthetic inputs, median of four settings, each the median slowest rank over 40 samples (single settings spiked up to 5.15 ms on the shared worker), 16384 x 4096 (ms) | 0.75/0.75 | 0.74/0.73 | closed |
| Plan, 16384 x 8192 (ms) | 1.15/1.11 | 1.09/1.09 | open |
| Plan, 16384 x 8192, 8 half-cached requests (ms) | 1.19/0.73 | 0.94/0.72 | open |
| Plan, 16384 x 16384 (ms) | 1.30/1.73 | 1.42/1.72 | open |

## Deliberate limits

- The test does not reach the 4096-row, 100 million, capture, or context parallelism checks.
- The test allows fewer than 5 differing rows, because a tie at the cutoff can swap a group. With `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2` off, the probe saw up to 6, unchecked for ties.

These limits are deliberate. Do not add code for them without a real input that reaches the case.

## Checklist

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.

## Codex Review Summary This comment shows the latest Codex review activity on this pull request. | Review | Status | Commit | Review trigger | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 📝 **Code Review** | ✅ **Completed** 2026-10-15T05:25:23.966287Z | `be489d2` | Draft marked ready |
ℹ️ About Codex in GitHub
[Your team has set up Codex to review pull requests in this repo](https://chatgpt.com/codex/cloud/settings/general). Reviews are triggered when you - Open a pull request for review - Mark a draft as ready - Comment "@codex review" or "@codex security review". Codex reacts with 👀 while any review is running, comments if it has suggestions, and reacts with 👍 once all reviews finish with no findings.

I compared replicated and sharded `_kpool_topk_by_row_chunks` at `f360044a9f` on four NVLink-connected B200s. This ran the PR’s row slicing, FP8 MQA logits, CUDA top-k transform and in-place NCCL gather, not a mocked collective. The inputs were synthetic: three requests, nonzero key offsets, 32 query heads of width 128, 2,048 pooled keys, `kpool=4`, `topk=512`, and 1,024-row budget chunks. Runtime: PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, NCCL 2.29.7, DeepGEMM 2.8.0.

| Input | Replicated | Sharded | Output |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 4,097 rows, shared page table with request indices, 7 padding rows | 0.325 ms | 0.267 ms | Same selected set on every row. All padding stayed `-1`. |
| 4,097 rows, per-query page table, 2 padding rows | 0.310 ms | 0.251 ms | Same selected set on every row. All padding stayed `-1`. |
| 16,384 rows, ragged offsets | 0.814 ms | 0.370 ms | One boundary tie described below. |

The sharded output was byte-identical across ranks within each gather. I would **not** require byte-identical top-k order across separate forwards: it varied even between two replicated passes. On ragged row `7462`, groups `90` and `156` also traded the last selected slot. Both logits had FP32 bits `0x428e664e`, with exactly 127 groups strictly above them and two tied for place 128. The same set difference occurred on the replicated control without sharding. A parity test should distinguish a tie at the cutoff from a missing or misordered query row.

Timings are median slowest-rank CUDA-event times over interleaved warm passes, including the gather. They measure the row method, not server prefill latency. The full planner, model accuracy and other TP sizes remain untested here.

+"""K-pool prefill row sharding on real TP ranks, compared with the replicated path."""
+
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import torch
+import torch.multiprocessing as mp
+
+from sglang.srt.distributed.parallel_state import (
+    GroupCoordinator,
+    init_distributed_environment,
+    initialize_model_parallel,
+)
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.dsa import dsa_indexer_kpool as indexer_module
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.dsa.dsa_topk_backend import TopkTransformMethod
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.dsa.kpool_plan import init_kpool_extend_metadata
+from sglang.srt.model_executor.forward_batch_info import ForwardMode
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_forward
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase, publish_build_topology
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=60, stage="extra-b", runner_config="4-gpu-b200")
+
+WORLD = 4
+
+
+@dataclass
+class _Metadata:
+    topk_indices_offset: torch.Tensor
+    kpool_extend_plan: object = None
+
+
+def _run_rank(rank, init_method):
+    torch.cuda.set_device(rank)
+    init_distributed_environment(WORLD, rank, init_method, local_rank=rank)
+    publish_build_topology(tp_size=WORLD, world_rank=rank)
+    initialize_model_parallel()
+    device = torch.device(f"cuda:{rank}")
+
+    # 12289 rows behind a cached prefix do not divide evenly across TP ranks,
+    # and q_fp8 has padding rows past them.
+    prefix, length, pad_rows = 20480, 32769, 5
+    n_real, pages = length - prefix, length // 256
+    batch = SimpleNamespace(
+        forward_mode=ForwardMode.EXTEND,
+        batch_size=1,
+        req_pool_indices=torch.tensor([1], device=device),
+        seq_lens=torch.tensor([length], device=device),
+        seq_lens_cpu=torch.tensor([length]),
+        extend_seq_lens_cpu=[n_real],
+        attn_cp_metadata=None,
+    )
+    metadata = SimpleNamespace(
+        attn_metadata=init_kpool_extend_metadata(
+            _Metadata(torch.zeros(n_real, device=device, dtype=torch.int32)),
+            batch,
+            kpool=4,
+            physical_page_size=64,
+            index_page_size=64,
+            topk_transform_method=TopkTransformMethod.RAGGED,
+            full_real_page_table=torch.arange(
+                pages * 4 + 4, device=device, dtype=torch.int32
+            )[None],
+            full_seqlens_expanded=torch.arange(
+                prefix + 1, length + 1, device=device, dtype=torch.int32
+            ),
+        ),
+        topk_transform_method=TopkTransformMethod.RAGGED,
+    )
+    # The same seed on every rank, because attention TP replicates inputs.
+    torch.manual_seed(7)
+    keys = torch.randn((pages + 1, 64, 128)).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).view(torch.uint8)
+    scales = (torch.rand((pages + 1, 64)) + 0.5).view(torch.uint8)
+    buf = torch.cat([keys.flatten(1), scales.flatten(1)], dim=1).to(device)
+    q_fp8 = torch.randn((n_real + pad_rows, 32, 128)).to(device, torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    weights = torch.rand((n_real + pad_rows, 32, 1)).to(device)
+    pool = SimpleNamespace(
+        index_page_size=64, get_index_k_with_scale_buffer=lambda layer_id: buf
+    )
+    indexer = object.__new__(indexer_module.IndexerKPool)
+    indexer.index_kpool, indexer.index_topk = 4, 2048
+
+    def topk(enabled, q_rows):
+        with envs.SGLANG_OPT_USE_DSA_KPOOL_PREFILL_TP.override(enabled):
+            return indexer._get_topk_ragged_kpool_plan(
+                batch, 0, q_fp8[:q_rows], weights[:q_rows], metadata
+            )
+
+    # Without padding rows the gather needs more rows than the output. The small
+    # logits budget splits each rank's rows across row chunks.
+    for q_rows, budget_bytes in ((n_real, 1 << 40), (n_real + pad_rows, 1 << 26)):
+        with (
+            patch.object(indexer_module, "get_token_to_kv_pool", return_value=pool),
+            patch.object(
+                indexer_module, "mqa_logits_budget_bytes", return_value=budget_bytes
+            ),
+            patch.object(
+                indexer_module.IndexerKPool,
+                "_fp8_mqa_logits",
+                wraps=indexer_module.IndexerKPool._fp8_mqa_logits,
+            ) as logits,
+            patch.object(
+                GroupCoordinator,
+                "all_gather_into_tensor",
+                autospec=True,
+                side_effect=GroupCoordinator.all_gather_into_tensor,
+            ) as gather,
+        ):
+            replicated = topk(False, q_rows)
+            gather.assert_not_called()
+            logits.reset_mock()
+            sharded = topk(True, q_rows)
+            scored = sum(c.kwargs["q_fp8"].shape[0] for c in logits.call_args_list)
+            assert scored <= (n_real + WORLD - 1) // WORLD, f"scored {scored} rows"
+            with get_forward().scoped(attn_input_scattered=True):
+                topk(True, q_rows)
+            gather.assert_called_once()
+
+        # Top-k order is not stable, and an equal score at the cutoff can swap a
+        # selected group, so a few rows may differ. A misplaced shard moves thousands.
+        same = (sharded.sort(dim=-1).values == replicated.sort(dim=-1).values).all(
+            dim=-1
+        )
+        assert (~same).sum() < 5, f"{(~same).sum()} rows differ"
+        # A tie keeps the row's width, while a row no rank scored stays all -1.
+        assert ((sharded < 0).sum(-1) == (replicated < 0).sum(-1)).all()
+
+
+class TestPrefillTPRows(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_sharded_path_matches_replicated_on_tp_ranks(self):
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="kpool-tp-") as tmp:
+            mp.spawn(_run_rank, args=(f"file://{tmp}/init",), nprocs=WORLD)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

I compared replicated and sharded `_kpool_topk_by_row_chunks` at `f360044a9f` on four NVLink-connected B200s. This ran the PR’s row slicing, FP8 MQA logits, CUDA top-k transform and in-place NCCL gather, not a mocked collective. The inputs were synthetic: three requests, nonzero key offsets, 32 query heads of width 128, 2,048 pooled keys, `kpool=4`, `topk=512`, and 1,024-row budget chunks. Runtime: PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, NCCL 2.29.7, DeepGEMM 2.8.0.

| Input | Replicated | Sharded | Output |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 4,097 rows, shared page table with request indices, 7 padding rows | 0.325 ms | 0.267 ms | Same selected set on every row. All padding stayed `-1`. |
| 4,097 rows, per-query page table, 2 padding rows | 0.310 ms | 0.251 ms | Same selected set on every row. All padding stayed `-1`. |
| 16,384 rows, ragged offsets | 0.814 ms | 0.370 ms | One boundary tie described below. |

The sharded output was byte-identical across ranks within each gather. I would **not** require byte-identical top-k order across separate forwards: it varied even between two replicated passes. On ragged row `7462`, groups `90` and `156` also traded the last selected slot. Both logits had FP32 bits `0x428e664e`, with exactly 127 groups strictly above them and two tied for place 128. The same set difference occurred on the replicated control without sharding. A parity test should distinguish a tie at the cutoff from a missing or misordered query row.

Timings are median slowest-rank CUDA-event times over interleaved warm passes, including the gather. They measure the row method, not server prefill latency. The full planner, model accuracy and other TP sizes remain untested here.
